title: Anchor-smoothing microburst scratchpad
content:
Goal: experiment with an "anchor-smoothing" control to reduce p99/p999 during short, high-amplitude microbursts without sacrificing steady-state throughput.

Summary of approach:
- Problem: very short (~1-6s) burst waves create KV/cache churn + immediate batching spikes that push p99 out by 30-70% vs baseline.
- Idea: maintain a lightweight EWMA 'anchor' of recent arrival rate and use a short smoothing window to avoid immediately dropping batching/priority lanes when a single mini-burst arrives. The anchor decays on configurable half-life.

Experiment setup:
- Cluster: 4x A100-80GB (Nanoslice), serving redwood/open-7b (int8) on CUDA 12.2 runtime.
- Inference config: max_tokens=512, max_concurrency=24, async batching enabled, dynamic batch timeout 12ms baseline.
- Workload generator: custom harness (wrk-like) with arrival schedule: background Poisson at 85 QPS, injected bursts: 3s triangular peaks to 420 QPS every 60s (mimics client traffic sampled from prod).
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency (server edge), 95th token tail, throughput (tokens/sec), request success ratio, observed scheduler queue depth.

Control knobs tried:
- EWMA alpha: 0.05, 0.15, 0.3 (maps to ~20s, 7s, 3s responsiveness)
- Smoothing window + hysteresis: fixed windows 3s/8s/20s plus a small cooldown so we don't oscillate quickly.
- Batch timeout adaptation: allow anchor to increase batch timeout by up to +8ms when anchor indicates imminent burst.

Notable single-run numbers (representative):
- Baseline (no smoothing): p50=45ms, p95=130ms, p99=410ms, p999=980ms, tokens/sec=11.2k.
- Anchor EWMA alpha=0.15, window 8s: p50=47ms, p95=123ms, p99=320ms, p999=640ms, tokens/sec=10.9k.
- Anchor alpha=0.3 (very responsive): p50=50ms, p95=140ms, p99=360ms, tokens/sec=10.7k (more conservative batching increased p50/p95).
- Alpha=0.05 (very slow): p50=44ms, p95=132ms, p99=395ms, tokens/sec=11.15k (minimal effect on tails).

Quick observations:
- Best tradeoff observed around alpha=0.15 + 8s smoothing: ~22% p99 improvement, ~35% reduction in p999, ~2.7% throughput loss. This seems OK for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Faster anchors (alpha>=0.3) react too aggressively and effectively treat microbursts as sustained load; they reduce tail less and hurt p50.
- Slower anchors (alpha<=0.05) don't help; they feel like no-op for 3-6s bursts.
- Hysteresis/cooldown is critical. Without a 6-10s cooldown we oscillate between modes multiple times inside a burst and see higher tail variance.
- Interplay with KV cache: increasing batching during the immediate rise keeps KV cache hits higher (less eviction churn), seems to be a hidden benefit for multi-request contexts.

Anomalies / noise seen:
- On one run there was a GC spike on host-2 (python wrapper) which skewed p999. Need to run more seed repeats.
- On longer runs (30 min), sustained small bursts cause the anchor to drift upward and then we need a forced decay path; otherwise it becomes the equivalent of a persistent scaling up and degrades steady-state latency.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Run 10-seed A/B with and without smoothing across two instance shapes (A100 vs H100) to confirm generality.
- Add metric: eviction-rate and per-tenant KV miss correlation to tails.
- Test with different batch timeout caps (+4ms and +12ms) to map latency/throughput frontier.
- Consider hybrid: anchor+short predictive model (simple linear predictor on last 3s) to detect true multi-second ramps vs single spike.
- Draft a short RFC describing anchor smoothing with config knobs and recommended defaults for hosted API endpoints (low-latency tier).

Notes to self: keep results as median of 5 runs before sharing; add small plot (arrival vs p99) to PR description. Also flag to SRE: ensure no external autoscaler kicks in during experiments (seen once).

Unresolved questions:
- How does smoothing interact with tenant-level fairness? If anchor increases batch timeout for one tenant, does it unfairly penalize co-tenants on same GPU? Maybe need per-tenant anchors + global safety cap.
- Is there a bounded worst-case where smoothing makes queueing unbounded under pathological repeated bursts? Need formal bound or safety limit.

Scratch commands used:
- ./bench --model open-7b-int8 --profile burst-triangular --qps-background 85 --burst-peak 420 --burst-duration 3 --period 60 --concurrency 24 --batch-timeout 12
- curl -X POST https://local-harness/driver/anchor?alpha=0.15&window=8&cooldown=8

End notes: promising quick win. Anchor-smoothing looks like a low-effort control with decent p99 gains for short microbursts; requires more seeds and safety checks before pushing to canary.
